notes.title: Season of Chaos Free Update: Unleash your new Buddy!
notes.notes:
Greetings, zombie-slayers! The [b]Season of Chaos free update[/b] descends upon you, bringing today a new best friend in the fight against the undead.

[h3]🐾 DLCorgi - Your New Free Buddy Companion, Available NOW![/h3]

Meet your adorable yet fierce four-legged companion, DLCorgi! Ready to take on the meanest Freddies, DLCorgi is the perfect sidekick to accompany you.

Update your game for free today, head to the Cosmetics screen, and select DLCorgi as your new trusty ally.

[previewyoutube=JD3i0MO4eLM;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]🔥 Even More Chaos - New Horde Mode Maps[/h3]

Unlock the next level of multiplayer mayhem with three brand-new Horde mode maps, dropping free of charge one each month from March to May. Gather your squad, hunker down, and face relentless waves of zombies together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44156130/eaf9e2fb1b89dc65fcc3b1fbba3deb90811ea147.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Get ready for the cold with After the Fall's Reclamation Update!

notes.title: Trailer Park Horde Mode map - Beta release
notes.notes:
The [i][b]Trailer Park[/b][/i] horde mode map will transport up to four players to a closed off-area set in a grungy lot full of scruffy old trailers. Gather your fellow survivors and watch each others’ back as you scavenge the rundown trailers for precious loot and explore the alleyways and narrow side streets in a map with many places to hide… or get ambushed. Stand your ground against wave after wave of undead Freddies for as long as you can.

[previewyoutube=j80onfXDyy0;full][/previewyoutube]

This beta release is available for all owners of Arizona Sunshine and can be accessed by opting into the "Trailerpark_Beta" branch via the Arizona Sunshine properties

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8824504/e324b28e5026c836a5c5042af6003153d589b4d7.png[/img]

We're very happy you're still killing zombies in our scorched apocalypse, and we're always reading what you have to say. The update for this map in the release build will follow in early January. Thanks for playing Arizona Sunshine!

notes.title: Patch notes: Get a grip!
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, we have some additional updates and fixes for Arizona Sunshine. These address the issues of equipment dropping and weapon gripping. Here are the patch notes for version 1.9.21017.

[list]
[*] The "Can drop equipment" setting is now disabled by default, even when Valve Index controllers are connected.
[*] Fixed equipment not being saved, between level loads and at checkpoints, when "Can drop equipment" was enabled.
[*] Fixed a bug where items would unequip from a hand right after loading a level if the player held an item in that hand in the previous level.
[*] Fixed a bug where hands could no longer equip items after they unequipped a mounted item by outranging it.
[*] Fixed not being able to pick up items after throwing them and then picking them up before they've come to a complete stop.
[*] The 'Can drop equipment' grip tutorials now show on both hands when they're both holding items.
[*] The flashlight is now a headlight in two-handed mode when 'Can drop equipment' is enabled.
[/list]

[u]Other updates[/u]
[list]
[*] Fixed the calibration text being clipped on some languages.
[*] Fixed Oculus Rift S controllers not allowing you to change rotation mode.
[*] Fixed the last voice over line in the Sunshine level always playing in the English language.
[/list]

Please update Arizona Sunshine to the latest version (1.9.21017) for these changes to be added. You can always leave your feedback here in the Steam forums, or on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/ZvdE9Bf]official Discord Channel[/url]. Thank you for your patience.

notes.title: Arizona Sunshine - Index Update
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/8824504/ef14424007d108c57fdffd49f53aeaa0f060d3eb.png[/img]

Hi everyone, 

We are eager to share a new update with you all. By popular demand, we have added a new feature that allows players to drop their guns and other equipment. By enabling this option you can grab and hold items by applying pressure to the force sensor in the grip of the Index controller, and drop items by releasing the grip, offering a more realistic and comfortable Index controller experience. The option is enabled by default for Index controllers and can also be enabled for all other supported controllers. You can find this setting in the gameplay menu. 

In addition, we also made the following updates:

[list]
[*]Fixed issue where Vive wand users could not use one or either of their triggers
[*]Fixed holstering in the first level
[*]Fixed WMR teleport aim rotation
[*]Hyperkin movement now working with sliding locomotion
[/list]

notes.title: Two-Handed Weapons Update Live
notes.notes:
Simultaneously with the launch of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/850210/Arizona_Sunshine__Dead_Man_DLC/]Arizona Sunshine - Dead Man DLC[/url] today, the free Two-Handed Weapons Update is now available for all Arizona Sunshine players!

Jump back into the zombie apocalypse armed with 13 new two-handed weapons in Two-Handed Mode, which supports play with regular VR motion controllers as well as VR peripherals including the PP Gun and the yet to be launched Arena Infinity™ LITE.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/271c39ac320283f80aadfbe0a4d253bb6c6e21d9.jpg[/img]

The update also includes a networking overhaul, improving multiplayer stability and adding a custom-built cross-platform matchmaking system that now also allows the matchmaking between Steam and Oculus Home players. 

Additionally, the patch adds Windows Mixed Reality controller support, adds Hyperkin Blaster support, and includes a variety of fixes for issues related to graphics, physics and gameplay.

Enjoy playing and let us know what you think below!

notes.title: Dead Man DLC gets a release-date!
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/837dfa574be4f67e43d73bbb027037150afbeab2.jpg[/img]

Hey all, 

On May 24th, the first campaign DLC for Arizona Sunshine will be coming to Oculus Rift, Vive and Windows Mixed Reality HMDs! We've just launched its [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/850210/Arizona_Sunshine__Dead_Man_DLC]Steam page[/url], so make sure to go add it to your wishlists.

Dead Man DLC adds a prequel mission set in a completely new environment that plays out in the final days before the events of Arizona Sunshine. In this mission, which is for the most part set in a missile silo, you head a frantic attempt by US Army Special Forces to launch a nuclear-warhead loaded missile vital to stopping the spread of zombies in the American Southwest.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/4794cb31d34459b38f26200b5f0fd1e47bddb207.png[/img]

This is desperate mission that will keep the most seasoned of Arizona Sunshine survivors on their toes! So, we're arming you with three new weapons: a fully automatic submachine gun, a two-handed shotgun and a tactical handgun.

Similarly to the main campaign, Dead Man DLC supports 2 player co-op play and various difficulty levels including the much-dreaded Apocalyptic Mode.

Also included are new masks matching the setting and we're introducing a couple of light customization options as well. Last but not least, new achievements! There's six of them for you to unlock.

Arizona Sunshine: Dead Man DLC will be available for $2.49. Wishlist it now on the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/850210/Arizona_Sunshine__Dead_Man_DLC]Dead Man DLC Steam page[/url] & leave your thoughts in the comments below.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/4274b143eb90b03bb8a967a0a353f788a3065475.png[/img]

notes.title: Two-Handed Update lumbering towards PC
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/d77525c5af974a8f6e0d44261ede94c71aa86a78.jpg[/img]

Hey all, another batch of free downloadable content is coming soon to your favorite VR zombie shooter, and with it support for various peripherals including the PP Gun and Omni, as well as a complete networking overhaul!

Read on to get the lowdown…

[h1]Two-handed mode[/h1]
We are excited to announce we have partnered with the folks over at Shenzhen Simeng Technology to support the [url=http://www.ppgun.com/bbx/en.html]PP Gun[/url], their two-handed gun-shaped VR controller for HTC Vive. With it, we will finally be able to bring two-handed mode to PC!

Originally developed with the PS VR Aim Controller (Sony’s two-handed VR gun) in mind, two-handed mode has you survive with 13 new two-handed weapons. Arizona Sunshine is all about shooting, so we wanted to provide the best experience when it comes to two-handed weapon support – with the PP Gun, we were able to get it exactly right. Of course, we realize not everyone will have a PP Gun at their disposal, nor play on HTC Vive. Therefore, two-handed mode will also be playable with regular motion controllers on both Oculus and HTC Vive – just be aware that it was designed with a two-handed gun peripheral in mind.
 
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/271c39ac320283f80aadfbe0a4d253bb6c6e21d9.jpg[/img]

[h1]Omni support[/h1]
Giving new meaning to walking dead, Omni support is expected to arrive with the next big update as well.

[h1]Networking overhaul[/h1]
In the mean time, we are also working on a huge overhaul of the matchmaking system on PC. With our latest VR game, [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/342190/Skyworld]Skyworld[/url], we invested in a custom-built cross-platform matchmaking back-end built from the ground up, which we always intended to bring over to Arizona Sunshine once finalized. This new system will allow you to directly match and play with users from the leading PC store platforms, including Steam and Oculus. We also expect this will make network connections between players more robust. 

At the moment, we cannot comment on an ETA for the update other than 'soon' yet as we do not want to set expectations that we are not 100% sure we can meet. Such is the nature of game development! Stay tuned or subscribe to the [url=http://arizona-sunshine.com]newsletter[/url] to be the first to get updates.

notes.title: Free Content Update Out Now: Undead Valley
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/90ca587e5812c8e0be87681127b417cb062e5640.jpg[/img]

[h1]The Freds have jumped the border in an all-new map![/h1]

We are delighted to introduce a brand-new Horde mode map to Arizona Sunshine! [b]Undead Valley[/b] takes you to a zombie-infested old transport warehouse-turned-underground casino in close proximity to Sin City, Nevada.

And you haven't even heard the best part: Undead Valley is available entirely [b]free of charge right now.[/b]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/9de81260beb90057884d7e013c15b5c193baaad7.jpg[/img]

Originally debuted at the Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas last January, Undead Valley will have a few surprises in store for even the most hardened zombie apocalypse-veterans among you. Read on below for some survival tips ([i]don't worry, it won't count as cheating[/i])...

[list]
[*]Undead Valley adds an [b]all-new Horde mode map[/b] in a location that you haven't seen before.
[*]The key to survival above all else is to [b]keep moving[/b] and take advantage of the map's indoor and outdoor areas as well as the verticality it adds to Horde mode.
[*]Expand your playground by retrieving keys to locked doors and blowing up obstacles in your way to [b]access new resources and tactical positions[/b].
[*]The waves of Freds that you've come to expect in Horde mode have made way for a [b]continuous onslaught of zombies[/b]: prepare for the ultimate challenge to test your VR survival skills!
[/list]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/5d7360a7b142288f4dd2a2ad6e34a4c3b13efbc2.jpg[/img]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/84ca4167cf523752db26da7ff6cc6a070b88452f.jpg[/img]

What do you think? Share your experience with us here, on Reddit or on [url=http://facebook.com/ArizonaSunshine]Facebook[/url] and [url=http://twitter.com/Vertigo_Games]Twitter[/url].

notes.title: Patch r1.4.7890
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We pushed the patch that was on the public test for two weeks live to the main branch in preparation for new builds.

It is a small patch in changes, but unfortunately a large patch in data. This is a result of the engine we are using and the complexity of the project. 

This patch includes the following changes:
- Walking locomotion smooth rotation speed is now faster
- The networking matchmaker now has a longer timeout, in cases where loading screens are long this should avoid disconnects.

We have some fixes in the pipeline, including:
- Gun Collect achievement fix
- Locomotion walking speed
- Left-handed locomotion

It is a small patch in changes, but unfortunately a large patch in data. This is a result of the engine we are using and the complexity of the project. 

This patch includes the following changes:
- Walking locomotion smooth rotation speed is now faster
- The networking matchmaker now has a longer timeout, in cases where loading screens are long this should avoid disconnects.

We have some fixes in the pipeline, including:
- Gun Collect achievement fix
- Locomotion walking speed
- Left-handed locomotion

notes.title: Patch 1.3.7750
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We are happy to present you with the latest patch. We have tried to address all the issues that have been reported since launch. Unfortunately we have not been able to reduce the crashes completely, due to a bug in the engine version we are using. We are in contact with the engine developers and will resolve this asap ( holidays are in the way ). Nevertheless, the crashes should not occur as often.

Happy holidays!


[h1]Key changes[/h1]
- Matchmaking has been adjusted, it should now be easier to find a match
- The extreme lag in later waves of the Horde Mode has been fixed
- Apocalyptic mode has received a save file. You can now progress level per level, also ammo placement has been adjusted
- The loading screen crashes should occur less frequent

[h1]General[/h1]
- Matchmaking has been adjusted, it should now be easier to find a match
- The loading screen crashes should occur less frequent
- Added and fixed glowsights for all guns
- The blackhawk gun animations have been fixed, the hand does not hide anymore
- Audio prioritization has been adjusted
- X,Y,A,B all reload the guns now on Touch controls
- High-end effects are not enabled by default anymore for all specs ( they can still be toggled )
- The chamber exit of the Forty Cal should now throw empty shells out in a more realistic direction
- Audio settings have been added to the settings screen
- When launching in mixed reality mode, the rendering is now set to Forward so all the quadrants render correctly.
- Explosive barrels are now correctly synced

[h1]Campaign[/h1]
- Zombie flickering should not happen anymore in the Base level
- Apocalyptic mode has received a save file. You can now progress level per level, also ammo placement has been adjusted
- The sniper and minigun can not be saved in a checkpoint anymore as starting equipment

[h1]Horde Mode[/h1]
- If a player disconnects in multiplayer, the sessions is not closed anymore
- In multiplayer the score is shared in the end for all players in the session
- Hamburgers now also regenerate health during intermissions
- The horde mode cartridge now is a single cartridge for both single and multiplayer.
- The extreme lag in later waves when using the shotgun has been fixed
- Fixed the issue where zombies could not find a target when the Flare was thrown by player #4

notes.title: VR shooter Arizona Sunshine has features locked behind timed CPU exclusivity [update: not any more]
notes.notes:
Update: Following widespread condemnation of Arizona Sunshine's timed exclusive content, the studio has announced that it's rolling back the limitations. In other words, there's no longer any exclusivity at all.

Here's the full statement:

Thank you for all your feedback on the game. We developed the game to be as immersive and engaging as we could. While we love to hear about the things that delight you, we also take to heart the things that we can do better. It’s clear from your feedback many of you are not happy with the previously undisclosed modes being available only on certain higher end PCs. You are most important to us, and we hear your comments. We are unlocking these modes immediately to all players, and we hope you enjoy them.

We have recommended and still recommend using the Core i7 in order to maintain a constant 90FPS with advanced physics. We also realize that these chips cost money. We created bonus content that was not advertised as a reward for those of you who took us up on our recommendation.

We wanted you to feel it was worth it, but we also wanted everybody to be able to play these modes eventually. These surprise game modes were meant to be a reward for those players with high-end VR systems who were looking for the most immersive experience possible.

You are most important to us, and we hear and appreciate your comments. We are unlocking these modes to all players immediately via an automatic update, and we hope you enjoy them. 

Original story:

Arizona Sunshine is a newly released VR FPS set in a post-apocalyptic desert landscape riddled with zombies. It's currently sitting on a "Mostly Positive" rating on Steam, and based on a cursory glance at the community forums, the game has a decent enough following. 

But not all is well in this particular zombie apocalypse: some users are annoyed that two of the game's modes are exclusive to PCs running 5th, 6th and 7th generation Intel Core i7 CPUs. Both singleplayer Horde mode and the ultra-difficult Apocalyptic Mode are exclusive to i7 CPU owners until March 6 next year.

To the best of my knowledge – and to the best of several other PC Gamer scribes' knowledge – a game has never had content exclusivity based on hardware components before. The likes of Nvidia HairWorks improves cosmetic aspects, such as in The Witcher 3, but that's a far cry from locking off playable in-game content to incentivise purchasing a high-end CPU.

The thing is, it appears that no word was given in advance that this exclusivity existed, though there's plenty of videos promoting the benefits of an i7 when playing the game, such as this trailer and this behind-the-scenes dev video. 

Responding to a concerned user in the game's Steam forums, a Vertigo Games spokeperson explained the situation. "These are two game modes that we have not focused on previously," the statement said. "Working with Intel allowed us to create even more content than we originally planned, including these modes and the physics systems in the game, making Arizona Sunshine one of the richest VR experiences possible. 

"We want to give 5th, 6th and 7th gen Intel Core i7 owners first glimpse into these additional modes, but they’ll be available March 6, 2017 to everyone who owns the game."

It's an unprecedented move, which might have been more acceptable had prospective purchasers of the game known about it. I've sent an Intel rep an email, and will update the story if I hear back.

notes.title: Release Date, Pre-order, & Closed Beta Update
notes.notes:
It's finally here!

We have a release date, and you can pre-order now!

Arizona Sunshine releases on December 6, 2016 for HTC Vive and Oculus Rift with Touch support.

Priced at $39.99, the game is now available for pre-order at a 15% discount. Pre-orders will also receive an Arizona Sunshine compositor image for their headsets, a desktop background image, and concept art from the game. 

Can't wait for December? The closed beta is November 22-29. The cut-off to sign-up is November 15th, so we will notify the participants shortly after that. Sign up [url=www.arizona-sunshine.com] here[/url] .

Still want more? Check this out. [url=www.polygon.com/virtual-reality/2016/11/9/13563370/arizona-sunshine-hands-on-vr] Playing One of VR’s Most Violent and Exciting Games[/url] by Ben Kuchera.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/c30deecd15e6e0450c3cced5f41429984ecd3ae7.jpg[/img]
 
[b]i5 vs i7 CPU[/b] 

So what's the big deal here? You keep telling us about the i7 or equivalent processor and what it does, but what do I get with it? Why do I want it?

Well, believe it or not, when you have to run a game at 90FPS, you become GPU limited quickly. Using Unity, you also do not have PhysX acceleration on the GPU, so the best option for advanced physics is to use a multi-threaded and multi-core CPU. Because of the advanced physics involved to make the game feel as immersive and realistic as possible, we recommend gamers use a CPU like the Intel® Core™ i7 processor. 

The game plays normally with an i5 or equivalent, but if your CPU has the speed, cores, and threads, you can turn on the advanced physics. While you can technically try advanced physics without the latest, fastest CPU, we don't recommend it. The CPU would choke. We've tested it.

What's the big deal? Check it out here.

https://youtu.be/ic3EKqa8270

notes.title: The Refinery & Closed Beta Update
notes.notes:
As announced in last week's newsletter (sign up @ www.arizona-sunshine.com ), the closed beta will consist of the first four levels of the game, ending at the conclusion of the Ol' Dutchman Mine. It will start in November, and we will announce the specific dates in the near future along with the cutoff date for signing up.

Participants will be randomly selected from the newsletter subscriber list and must own an HTC Vive or have access to Oculus Touch to participate. You must also:

- Sign up with a valid email address
- Be 18 years of age
- Accept the invitation and terms of service within three days of being selected
- Have a Steam or an Oculus Home account

We have previously shared some details about the levels that will be included in the beta, but we don't want to end this post without sharing some info about a new level - The Refinery.
 
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/447d6a0f7261abd42f6cd12a7ae5faaa42c42c35.jpg[/img]

As you start the level, you notice something new. Signs of civilization.
 
All you have to do is get past a horde of zombies and that enormous wall. You just can't catch a break.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/8824504/c30deecd15e6e0450c3cced5f41429984ecd3ae7.jpg[/img]

This place looks like a fortress. Someone gets an A+ in zombie survival planning. It'd be nice if they're still around. All this zombie killing is tiring. Somebody else needs to start carrying some weight around here.
 
This is going to suck if nobody else is here to help. There are buildings, towers, storage tanks and pipes everywhere to search. 

Better get a move on. Standing around won't get you any closer to safety.
